children: U.S. natural gas inventories likely rose by more than usual last week, extending the storage surplus above the five-year average as the injection season draws to a close, according to a survey by The Wall Street Journal.

Gas in underground storage is expected to have increased by 32 billion cubic feet to 3,894 Bcf in the week ended Nov. 13, according to the average estimate of 12 analysts, brokers and traders. Estimates range from an injection of 25 Bcf to an injection of 68 Bcf.

The expected storage build compares with a five-year average for the week of 15 Bcf, and would increase the inventory surplus over the 2021-2025 average to 92 Bcf from 75 Bcf the week before. The weekly injection could be the last before the first winter withdrawals begin as seasonal heating demand picks up.
The Energy Information Administration is scheduled to report natural gas inventory data on Thursday at 10:30 a.m. ET.
